findings.finding: Centrus closed the Westerman Holdings acquisition on 2026-10-19 for about $116M ($95M cash, $21M stock), and the 2026-09-09 prospectus supplement says the target had about $160M of revenue in 2025. Westerman serves non-nuclear oil-and-gas customers as well as Centrus. Consolidating it from Oct 19 adds roughly $20-30M of external Q4 revenue that the reaffirmed $450-500M FY guide (set before the deal) and the Street's $470.6M likely do not include, so a raised or firmed FY revenue range on the call is plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-08-05 the FY guide was reaffirmed at $450-500M after an earlier raise from $425-475M, and the stock fell 5.12%. On 2026-05-05, the print where the guide was raised, it rose 12.27%.
findings.why_not_priced: The $160M figure sits in the Recent Developments section of a 424B5 for an unnamed target. The 2026-10-19 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001065059/000162828026066212/ex991_101926westermanpr.htm) gives no revenue figure and no guidance update. Earnings Whispers' 10-27 preview still carries FY consensus of $470.6M against the old guide. If the market had priced a mechanical revenue add, FY consensus would sit above the guide midpoint.
findings.independence: Two documents from the same company: the 424B5 for the revenue and the 8-K for the close and the oil-and-gas customer base. No independent source. The revenue is inorganic and low-margin, and the market may look through it.

findings.finding: Q2 2026 already showed cost pressure that carries into a seasonally light Q3 (consensus revenue $55-59M against $176.1M in Q2): SWU unit cost +13% y/y against SWU price +3%, Technical Solutions at a $1.7M gross loss, and net hiring targets raised to 175+ at Piketon and 100+ at Oak Ridge. UBS cut its target to $170 on higher operating costs, and Needham cut to $206 on earnings concerns. Q3 is therefore likely a GAAP loss or near-zero EPS against a bar that ranges from +$0.35 to -$0.75.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (2025-11-05), the last seasonally light quarter, reported diluted EPS of $0.19 against a $0.36 consensus and fell 14.72%. Q2 2026 beat on revenue and EPS and still fell 5.12%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The cost lines are public, the stock is -38% over 20 days, and the EPS bar is so dispersed that no single miss is defined. It is filed small and capped because the bar is disputed.
findings.independence: The analyst target cuts are reported at https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/centrus-energy-stock-hits-52week-low-at-968-usd-93CH-4992590 (2026-11-02) and in the Barchart UBS item. Both rest on the same Q2 cost lines, so this is one finding.

findings.finding: DOE said it does not intend to exercise further options on the HALEU Operation Contract. Its period of performance ran only to 2026-09-30 under a $15.0M fixed-price 3-month Option 1b with no production, and the proposed FY2027 DOE budget excludes it. About $0.8B of Technical Solutions backlog is exposed, and the Q3 10-Q is the first report after the expiry, so it will show whether that backlog is cut or converted into a commercial operating arrangement.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The DOE non-exercise language first appeared in the 2026-08-05 release, and the stock fell 5.12% that session alongside the other items.
findings.why_not_priced: The risk is disclosed. What is not public is the treatment: a $0.8B backlog write-down would make the reported backlog fall even as LEU bookings rise. Size is net of the rest of the company: Technical Solutions was about $23M of Q2's $176M.
findings.independence: ANS / Power coverage of the contract restructuring: https://www.ans.org/news/2026-07-06/article-8180/doe-contract-boosts-centruss-haleu-goals-as-urenco-continues-leu-expansion/

findings.finding: Three LEU/HALEU supply agreements with prepayments were signed inside Q3: X-energy (2026-08-06), Radiant (2026-09-09) and Antares (2026-09-17), all with values undisclosed. The Q3 10-Q is the first document to quantify them in backlog (was $4.5B at June 30) and in customer advances (about $0.1B deferred revenue and advances at June 30).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog rose from $3.8B to $4.5B over H1 2026 while the stock fell 5.12% on the Q2 print, so backlog growth alone has not been bought. Contingent backlog is milestone-dependent.
findings.why_not_priced: Contract values and prepayment amounts were withheld in every release (Securities.io, WNN), so no one can model the backlog or cash-advance step. If they were priced, previews would quote a Q3 backlog estimate, and the 10-27 Earnings Whispers preview only lists backlog as a watch item.
findings.independence: Separate releases: Radiant and X-energy on the company news page (https://www.centrusenergy.com/news/category/news-releases/), WNN on Antares (https://www.world-nuclear-news.org/articles/antares-centrus-sign-multi-year-haleu-contract). Same company as the source, so not independent of it.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: about 29.7% of shares are sold short with 6.8 days to cover, and the stock sits at a fresh 52-week low ($96.80 on 11-02, $91.38 intraday 11-04). That is -38% in 20 days and less than half the $199.64 price of the $500M September equity raise. Market cap is about $1.98B, against roughly $2.1-2.2B of cash after the $489M net raise and the $95M Westerman payment, and $1.21B of convertible notes.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Large positive reactions have come when the setup was depressed: +33.13% (2025-02-06), +22.01% (2025-05-07) and +12.27% (2026-05-05). Three of the last four prints were down, though.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, not a fact the market lacks. It is filed as a squeeze mechanism if the guide holds, not as 'cheap'. The settlement date of the short reading is not shown on the page.
findings.independence: Market cap and 52-week low: https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/centrus-energy-stock-hits-52week-low-at-968-usd-93CH-4992590 (2026-11-02). Offering price: https://finviz.com/news/390546/centrus-announces-pricing-of-500-million-underwritten-public-offering-of-class-a-common-stock-and-warrants. findings.finding: The nuclear-sector sell-off is driven by rates: after the hot September CPI on 2026-10-14 the 10-year Treasury hit 5.26%, and Oklo and NuScale fell about 15% in a week. Centrus has fallen with the group despite near-term revenue, so a sector tape and not the print may still set the 11-05 session.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Centrus fell 4% on 2026-10-12 with the group, the smallest loss of the three names.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It is a proxy filed small because sector beta still acts inside the window.

findings.finding: Peer read-through: Cameco's Q3 2026, reported 2026-10-30 after Centrus last spoke, showed lower sales volumes and higher unit costs, missed EPS consensus, and showed the term uranium price at $96.50 and spot at $89.63 at quarter-end. Cameco also signed exclusive marketing of Global Laser Enrichment output, a future enrichment competitor targeting 2030.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of Centrus reacting to Cameco prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for four sessions. It is a proxy: Cameco is a miner and Centrus's SWU book is contracted, so transmission is weak.

outside_window.finding: First Investor Day is scheduled for December 2026. The multi-year outlook and the 2027 guide are likely saved for it, which lowers how much forward guidance the 11-05 call carries.

The Import Ban Act ends Russian LEU imports on 2028-01-01. Centrus has waivers for committed 2024-2027 deliveries, its third request (2026-2027 future sales) is still pending, and over half of LEU deliveries through 2027 are TENEX-sourced. No decision is dated inside the window.
